explanation: Compact non-b characters into the front while counting a characters. The final length is compacted length plus a count. Scan that compacted prefix backward, replacing each a by two d characters and copying other characters backward.
timeComplexity: O(size). Each active character is read a constant number of times and emits at most two characters.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: indices and counts only; the supplied buffer must have capacity for the expanded result. New-list variants store output explicitly; in-place variants use existing capacity and constant index state.

correctness: Forward compaction writes no farther than the read position, preserving unread input. The extra a count gives exactly enough output positions for expansion. Backward writing stays at or after the unread compacted prefix, so expansion cannot overwrite a character still needed. The returned length selects exactly the transformed prefix.
walkthrough: For size=5 and [a,c,b,a,e,"",""], forward compaction leaves [a,c,a,e] with two a characters, so final length is 6. Backward writes place e at 5, dd at 3..4, c at 2 and dd at 0..1. Return 6; the wrapper observes [d,d,c,d,d,e].
edgeCases: Unused buffer entries are never processed.
Every a expands to exactly two d characters.
Removing b can shrink the output even when expansion capacity exists.
